categories.name: Phase 1 · Foundations & Model Inference
categories.description: Understand what an AI engineer ships, then run real inference on pre-trained models — and reason about their token and cost behavior
outcomes: Explain how the AI-engineer role differs from ML engineer and data scientist
Call a hosted model and read its token and cost implications
Explain tokenization, attention and scaling laws in applied terms
Pick a model for a task by latency, cost and capability

categories.name: Phase 2 · Prompting & Structured Output
categories.description: Make model output reliable — prompts, tool/function calling, and schema-valid JSON
outcomes: Write system prompts and few-shot examples that hold under variation
Drive function/tool calls
Ship a Structured Data Extractor: text in, schema-validated JSON out (Portfolio L1)

categories.name: Phase 3 · Embeddings & RAG
categories.description: Ground answers in your own data — embeddings and retrieval with a vector database and a metadata store
outcomes: Embed and index a corpus with an embedding model
Tune chunking and retrieval strategies, then measure them
Ship a Document Q&A System with citations and a faithfulness/relevance eval (Portfolio L1)

categories.name: Phase 4 · Agents & Orchestration
categories.description: Build agents that reason and act — tool-use loops, multi-agent coordination, and orchestration
outcomes: Build a tool-using agent loop
Coordinate multiple agents and orchestrate multi-step work
Ship a Multi-Source Research Agent reusing Phase 2 tool calls and Phase 3 retrieval (Portfolio L2)

categories.name: Phase 5 · Long-Term Memory
categories.description: Give agents durable recall — semantic, episodic and procedural memory, context-window engineering, and long-term memory stores that survive across sessions
outcomes: Distinguish semantic vs episodic vs procedural memory and when each applies
Engineer the context window: compression, dynamic assembly, windowing
Persist long-term memory with vector + metadata stores (e.g. LangMem)

categories.name: Phase 6 · LangChain & LangGraph
categories.description: Build production agent graphs with LangChain and LangGraph — LCEL chains, stateful graphs, D1-checkpointed memory, human-in-the-loop, and tracing
outcomes: Compose LangChain runnables/LCEL chains with tools and retrievers
Model an app as a LangGraph StateGraph with D1 checkpointing and resume
Add human-in-the-loop interrupts and stream/trace a graph end to end
Ship a deployed multi-agent LangGraph service on the edge (Portfolio L2)

categories.name: Phase 7 · Evals, Safety & Observability
categories.description: Prove it works and ships safely — evals, red-teaming, guardrails, and gateway-level observability
outcomes: Build an eval suite (benchmarks + LLM-as-judge) that gates a model change
Add guardrails and mitigate hallucination and bias
Ship an eval + red-team + observability harness over your Phase 4–5 agent (Portfolio L3)

categories.name: Phase 8 · Ship to Production
categories.description: Take it to production — deploy, scale, cost-control, and CI/CD
outcomes: Deploy and scale a production service
Cap inference cost and wire CI/CD-gated evals
Ship a cost-bounded, observable AI feature to production (e.g. an AI Code Review Bot)

categories.name: Appendix · Fine-tuning & Training
categories.description: Optional track — customize models with LoRA, RLHF and dataset curation when prompting is not enough
outcomes: Decide when fine-tuning beats prompting, with a measured comparison
Fine-tune with LoRA/QLoRA on a curated dataset
Ship a domain-tuned assistant wrapped in a safety stack (Portfolio L3, senior signal)

categories.name: Appendix · Other Clouds & Platforms
categories.description: Optional track — GCP, Docker and Kubernetes for portability and comparison off the primary path
outcomes: Map serverless concepts onto GCP equivalents
Containerize a service with Docker
Run a workload on Kubernetes

categories.name: Appendix · Engineering & Communication
categories.description: Optional track — software-engineering foundations (SOLID, ACID, SQL, CI/CD) plus LlamaIndex and communication
outcomes: Apply SOLID design and ACID guarantees
Reason about microservices, SQL joins and CI/CD
Communicate technical work with structure and presence
